value_stream.name: Workforce Background Screening, Credentialing & Personnel Vetting

fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly analytics cycle; vendor performance review (W4867); governance reporting

workflows.name: Screening Operations Analytics — Volume, TAT, Hit-Rate, Vendor Performance

Automation Opportunity: - Screening-operations dashboard; TAT/coverage auto-monitor; vendor-performance scorecard
Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733: analytics reviewed quarterly; actions tracked to closure
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), W4867/W4884 (vendor), W4866 (policy), W4885 (cost), W4888 (improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Insight-inaction risk**: Analytics not acted on; mitigated by action-tracking
- **Coverage-blindspot risk**: An unscreened category/role undetected; mitigated by coverage-gap analytics
- **Vendor-underperformance risk**: A slow/inaccurate vendor not addressed; mitigated by vendor comparison
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); screening platform; HRIS (VS-19/103); procurement (VS-03); contingent workforce (VS-98)

steps.activity: Build the screening-operations analytics suite: screening volume by category (employee/contingent/vendor/executive) and role-tier, TAT by check-type/vendor, hit-rate (adverse findings) by check-type/role, re-screening currency, vendor performance (W4867), and cost (W4885)

Analyze & report: TAT vs SLA, bottleneck check-types, hit-rate trends (rising criminal/sanctions hits?), vendor comparison, coverage gaps (unscreened categories/roles), and the adverse-action outcome mix (clear/conditional/disqualify)
Feed insights to vendor governance (W4867/W4884), policy (W4866), resourcing, and continuous improvement (W4888); track action closure

fields.Owner: Screening Program Manager / LP (VS-23) / Corporate Security (VS-159)
fields.Trigger: Insider event (theft VS-23, fraud VS-125, security VS-159, workplace-violence); periodic correlation

workflows.name: Insider-Risk Linkage — Screening to LP/Fraud/Security Event Correlation

Automation Opportunity: - Event → screening-record correlation; insider-risk dashboard (VS-23/VS-159); control-improvement tracker
Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733 (every insider event screened-correlated; gaps remediated; evidence preserved (W4870))
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP), VS-125 (fraud), VS-159 (security), VS-21.2 (ERM), W4870 (evidence), W4877 (triggers), W4888 (governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Negligent-hiring liability risk**: An incident revealing a screening gap → civil liability; mitigated by post-incident review + evidence (W4870)
- **Correlation-blindspot risk**: Insider events not feeding back to screening improvements; mitigated by the linkage
- **Privacy risk**: Over-mining screening data post-incident; mitigated by lawful basis + minimization (W4868)
System Touchpoints: - LP/fraud (VS-23/VS-125); corporate security (VS-159); ERM (VS-21.2); screening evidence (W4870); analytics (VS-28); legal (VS-100.3)

steps.a: VP Legal & Compliance / Chief Compliance & Security Officer
steps.activity: On an insider event (theft/fraud/security/violence by an employee/contingent/vendor person), correlate to the individual's screening record (was the event foreseeable from screening? a gap? a missed check? a stale screen?) — a post-incident screening-review
steps.r: LP / Corporate Security / Screening Program Manager

steps.activity: Identify screening-program improvements: role-package gaps (W4869), re-screening gaps (W4877), source-quality issues (W4883), vendor failures (W4884), or consistency gaps (W4878); strengthen controls accordingly
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / LP / Corporate Security

steps.activity: Maintain the insider-risk-screening feed (W4877 triggers): insider-event learnings feed continuous monitoring and triggered re-vet; report correlation findings/trends to governance (W4888), ERM (VS-21.2), and analytics (W4881); support negligent-hiring defense with screening evidence (W4870)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Risk / LP / Legal

fields.Trigger: Suspect document; authenticity-check failure; fraud pattern; vendor source-quality issue
fields.Volume: ~30–60 suspect documents per year (subset of screens)

Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733: source-authentication for high-risk documents; fraud investigated; disqualification/legal action where warranted
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-104 (government affairs/systemic), W4867 (vendor), W4880 (adverse-action), W4881 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Forged-document risk**: A forged clearance letting an unfit person in → incident + negligent-hiring; mitigated by source-authentication
- **Verification-cost risk**: Verifying every document is costly; mitigated by risk-based verification + automation
- **False-allegation risk**: Wrongly flagging a genuine document; mitigated by source-confirmation
System Touchpoints: - Screening platform (verification); LP (VS-23); legal (VS-100.3); government portals (NBI/PRC/TESDA); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Detect false/forged documents: forged NBI clearances, fake police clearances, fabricated employment/education credentials, altered licenses (W1400/W4754/W600); use source-authentication (NBI portal verification, school/employer direct verification, PRC portal), document-forensics, and pattern-detection

Investigate & decide: verify via the issuing source, document the fraud, route to the Adverse-Action Board (W4880 — disqualification), and where material, escalate to LP (VS-23) and Legal (VS-100.3) for possible legal action (falsification of documents)

Manage vendor source-quality (W4867/W4884) and report fraud-trends (rising forgery?) to governance (W4888), analytics (W4881), and Government Affairs (VS-104) where systemic; strengthen verification controls

fields.Trigger: Vendor onboarding (W4867); periodic TPRM cycle; performance/quality/fraud issue

Automation Opportunity: - Vendor-performance/TPRM dashboard; concentration monitor; exit-plan tracker
Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733: vendors tiered & TPRM'd; performance monitored; concentration limits; exit planned
Cross-references: - links to VS-161 (TPRM), VS-86 (ABC), VS-91 (privacy/DPA), VS-100.3 (legal), W4867 (contract), W4870 (quality), W4881 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-failure risk**: A screening vendor failing (quality/breach/financial) disrupting the program; mitigated by TPRM + backup
- **Concentration risk**: Single-vendor criticality; mitigated by concentration limits
- **Data-handling-breach risk**: Vendor mishandling sensitive data (RA 10173); mitigated by DPA + cyber-attestation
System Touchpoints: - TPRM (VS-161); procurement (VS-03/VS-34); privacy (VS-91); ABC (VS-86); legal (VS-100.3); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Manage screening-vendor/agency risk per the enterprise TPRM (VS-161): tiering by criticality/sensitivity (screening providers handle criminal/credit data — high-sensitivity), cyber-attestation, financial DD, privacy/DPA compliance (W4867/W4868), concentration limits, and resilience/exit

Monitor vendor/agency performance & compliance (SLA W4870, accuracy W4883, ABC/anti-corruption VS-86, privacy VS-91, data-security), and manage issues (quality drop, fraud, breach) with corrective action or exit

Manage concentration/resilience: avoid single-vendor criticality, maintain backup capability, and plan exit (data return/destruction); feed vendor-risk to TPRM (VS-161), governance (W4888), and analytics (W4881)

fields.Trigger: Annual budget; quarterly cost review; vendor consolidation; ROI justification

workflows.name: Screening Cost & ROI Analytics — Spend, Loss-Avoided, Vendor Consolidation

Automation Opportunity: - Cost-ledger auto-feed; cost-per-hire analytics; vendor-consolidation model
Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733: cost reconciled to finance; ROI tracked; optimization risk-aware
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-03 (procurement), VS-161 (TPRM), W4867/W4884 (vendor), W4882 (loss-linked), W4881/W4888 (analytics/governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-leakage risk**: Duplicate/over-screening or over-paying vendors; mitigated by the cost ledger
- **ROI-invisibility risk**: Program cut as overhead without loss-avoided justification; mitigated by the ROI view (W4882)
- **Over-optimization risk**: Cost-cutting increasing risk; mitigated by risk-aware optimization
System Touchpoints: - Finance FP&A (VS-17.4); procurement (VS-03); analytics (VS-28); TPRM (VS-161); screening platform

steps.activity: Maintain the screening-cost ledger: vendor fees (W4867), agency screening costs (VS-98), internal staffing, drug/health (VS-83/VS-150), and license-verification costs; reconcile to finance (VS-17) by category/role-tier
Analyze cost & ROI: cost-per-screen, cost-per-hire, vendor comparison, consolidation opportunities, and the loss-avoided/loss-linked-to-screening-gaps (W4882) to justify the program; forecast spend

Drive cost optimization: consolidate vendors (W4867/W4884), negotiate volume pricing, automate (W4870/W4881), right-size packages (W4869 — avoid over-screening), and report cost/ROI to governance (W4888) and analytics (W4881)

fields.Owner: Screening Program Manager / Legal (VS-100.3) / DPO (VS-91) / Government Affairs (VS-104)
fields.Participants: HR Policy, Labor Relations (VS-84), Compliance Portfolio (VS-166)
fields.Trigger: Regulatory change (DOLE labor, NPC privacy RA 10173, NBI/PNP clearance rules, data-localization); legal change
fields.Volume: ~2–4 regulatory changes per year affecting screening

Automation Opportunity: - Regulatory-change feed; policy-update workflow; adoption tracker
Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733: regulatory changes logged & adopted; policy current; reported to governance
Cross-references: - links to VS-91 (privacy), VS-84 (labor), VS-104 (government affairs), VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-166 (compliance portfolio), W4866/W4868/W4872/W4880 (policy/consent/retention/adverse-action)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Change-blindspot risk**: A regulatory change missed → non-compliance; mitigated by multi-source monitoring
- **Slow-adoption risk**: Change identified but policy/operations not updated; mitigated by adoption tracking
- **Cross-border risk**: Foreign-worker screening/data-transfer rules (VS-160); mitigated by DPO review
System Touchpoints: - Legal (VS-100.3); privacy/DPO (VS-91); labor (VS-84); government affairs (VS-104); ERM (VS-21.2); compliance portfolio (VS-166)

steps.activity: Monitor regulatory change affecting screening: DOLE labor/OSH (W4879 drug-testing rules VS-150), NPC/RA 10173 (consent, retention, DSAR, breach — W4868/W4872), NBI/PNP clearance rules, PRC/TESDA verification, fair-chance/anti-discrimination developments, and cross-border data (W4879/VS-160)
steps.r: Legal / DPO / Government Affairs / Screening Program Manager

steps.activity: Assess impact & update policy (W4866): change consent language, retention rules, packages, or the adverse-action framework (W4880) to comply; communicate to HR/vendors/agencies
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Legal / DPO / HR Policy

steps.activity: Track adoption to closure and report to governance (W4888); capture emerging regulatory risk for ERM (VS-21.2) and the compliance portfolio (VS-166)

fields.Trigger: Annual internal-audit plan (VS-21); regulator audit; assurance cycle

workflows.name: Internal Audit Coordination, Control Testing & Compliance Assurance

Automation Opportunity: - Control-testing sample automation; finding-remediation tracker; controls-matrix sync
Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733: risk-based audit coverage; control testing; findings remediated & reported
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (internal audit), VS-36 (board), internal-controls matrix, VS-91 (privacy), W4868/W4870/W4880/W4884 (key controls), W4881/W4888 (analytics/improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Audit-finding-backlog risk**: Findings not remediated; mitigated by closure tracking
- **Control-gap risk**: A material control untested; mitigated by risk-based coverage
- **Privacy-control risk**: RA 10173 controls (consent/retention) not tested; mitigated by DPO involvement
System Touchpoints: - Internal audit (VS-21); internal-controls matrix; board governance (VS-36); privacy (VS-91); analytics (VS-28)
Time Estimate: - ~annual audit cycle weeks; remediation tracking continuous

steps.a: CHRO / VP Legal & Compliance / Head of Internal Audit
steps.activity: Coordinate the screening audit plan with Internal Audit (VS-21): risk-based coverage of consent (W4868), packages (W4869), chain-of-custody (W4870), adverse-action due process (W4880), retention (W4872), vendor governance (W4884), and coverage gaps (W4878); align with the internal-controls matrix
Support control testing: walkthroughs, sample testing (consent-before-screen, package-completeness, adverse-action due-process, retention-disposal, vendor-DPA), and remediation of findings
steps.r: Internal Audit / Screening Program Manager / HR / DPO

steps.activity: Track audit-finding remediation to closure, report to the audit & risk committee (VS-36), and feed findings to continuous improvement (W4888) and analytics (W4881)

fields.Owner: CHRO / Chief Compliance & Security Officer / Screening Program Manager
fields.Participants: Strategy (VS-33), Internal Audit (VS-21), OpEx (VS-133), HR, Security (VS-159)
fields.Trigger: Annual program review; maturity assessment; major incident (W4882); strategy refresh (W4865)

Controls: - CTL-733 (ensure controlled execution — Screening Analytics, Risk & Program Assurance (PA-167.3).)
- CTL-733: maturity assessed annually; improvement pipeline managed; benefit realized & reported
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-133 (OpEx), VS-28 (analytics), VS-36 (board), VS-21.2 (ERM), W4865 (strategy), W4882 (incidents), W4881 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stagnation risk**: Program not maturing/automating; mitigated by the maturity model + improvement pipeline
- **Over-engineering risk**: Automation without ROI; mitigated by benefit-realization tracking
- **Board-disconnect risk**: Material screening/insider risk not on the board radar; mitigated by quarterly reporting
System Touchpoints: - Strategy (VS-33); OpEx (VS-133); analytics (VS-28); board governance (VS-36); ERM (VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Assess program maturity across dimensions (coverage, package-design, consent/privacy, chain-of-custody/evidence, re-screening/continuous-monitoring, vendor-governance, analytics/automation, governance) using a maturity model; benchmark vs industry/peer
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Strategy / Internal Audit

steps.activity: Drive improvement: prioritize initiatives (automation W4870/W4881, coverage expansion, package right-sizing, vendor consolidation), execute via OpEx (VS-133), and track benefit realization

steps.a: CHRO / Chief Compliance & Security Officer / Board
steps.activity: Report program maturity, metrics, and incidents (W4882) to the board/audit & risk committee (VS-36); capture emerging best-practice and feed to ERM (VS-21.2)
